input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Absence confirmed by exhaustive search: no hits for "solicit", "induce", "recruit" (other than § 12.3's carve-out), "poach", or any restricted-period language ("twelve (12) months", "directly or indirectly" covenant), and the only affirmative "Customer shall not" obligation in the Agreement is § 13.4 (reverse engineering). Full reads of § 12 (Customer Responsibilities), § 16 (Confidentiality) and § 30 (General) — the sections where a non-solicit would sit — contain none. Accordingly no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Northwind, which is our preferred position ("no non-solicit on Customer"), and no redline or counterparty comment is proposed. Section 12.3 independently supports the finding: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" — the substantive equivalent of a general-solicitation/general-advertising carve-out — and records that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. The deterministic checks for a ≤ 12-month duration and a general-solicitation carve-out are heuristics keyed to an existing non-solicit covenant; with no covenant binding Customer they have nothing to measure and do not undercut compliance. Our fallback (mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire) would only be engaged if Vendor later proposes adding such a clause.
